concepts.name: Genesis and Launch of LiFE Mission
key_dimensions: PM Modi's proposal at COP26 Glasgow (November 2021) — exact context and framing
Formal global launch at Kevadiaya, Gujarat (October 2022) with UN Secretary-General Guterres
Distinction between proposal stage (COP26) and formal launch (2022) — a common UPSC trap
Role of UNEP as co-launch partner and institutional backing

concepts.name: Core Philosophy: 'Pro-Planet People' (P3)
key_dimensions: Shift from 'use-and-dispose' economy to circular, mindful consumption
P3 as the target community — definition, scope, and global ambition of 1 billion people
Contrast with traditional environmentalism: individual behaviour vs. systemic/policy change
Overlap and distinction with UN SDG-12 (Responsible Consumption and Production)

concepts.name: LiFE vs. Traditional Climate Frameworks (UNFCCC/Paris Agreement)
key_dimensions: Paris Agreement focuses on state-level NDCs; LiFE targets individual/household behaviour
LiFE as a demand-side complement to supply-side mitigation policies
How LiFE supports India's NDC commitments indirectly (e.g., reducing energy demand)
Risk of 'greenwashing' critique: shifting burden from industry to individuals

concepts.name: Seven Themes / Action Categories of LiFE
key_dimensions: Official seven themes: Save water, Save energy, Reduce waste, Reduce e-waste, Adopt sustainable food systems, Adopt healthy lifestyles, Reduce use of single-use plastic
UPSC trap: distinguishing LiFE themes from those of other missions (Swachh Bharat, Jal Shakti)
Mapping themes to existing government schemes (e.g., UJALA for energy, Jal Jeevan for water)
Which themes directly address India's Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs)

concepts.name: Institutional Architecture: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) as Nodal Ministry
key_dimensions: MoEFCC's role as the nodal ministry for LiFE implementation — not NITI Aayog or MEA
Inter-ministerial coordination mechanism required for cross-cutting themes
Role of UNEP India office in co-designing the implementation framework
Distinction from National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC) institutional structure

concepts.name: LiFE and India's Updated NDCs (2022)
key_dimensions: India's updated NDC: 45% emissions intensity reduction by 2030, 50% non-fossil electricity capacity
LiFE as a soft-power instrument to demonstrate demand-side climate leadership
How behavioural change in consumption can reduce import dependence on fossil fuels
Tension: India's per capita emissions are low — moral argument for LiFE vs. historical emitters

concepts.name: Global Coalition for LiFE
key_dimensions: India's push to build an international coalition of nations endorsing LiFE
G20 presidency (2023) used as platform to mainstream LiFE globally
New Delhi Leaders' Declaration (G20, 2023) and LiFE references
Distinction between symbolic endorsement by G20 vs. binding obligations

concepts.name: LiFE and the Concept of 'Mindful Consumption'
key_dimensions: Philosophical roots in Indian traditions: Gandhian simplicity, 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam'
Contrast with Western consumerism model and its climate externalities
UPSC angle: how Indian civilisational values are presented as global climate solutions
Critique: voluntary mindful consumption insufficient without regulatory frameworks

concepts.name: LiFE Portal and Digital Engagement Strategy
key_dimensions: Official LiFE portal and its 75 individual actions across seven themes
Use of social media campaigns, influencers, and MyGov platform for citizen mobilisation
Gamification and pledge-taking mechanisms — comparison with similar nudge-based policies
Data collection concerns: privacy vs. behavioural tracking for policy feedback

concepts.name: Single-Use Plastic (SUP) Ban and LiFE
key_dimensions: India's ban on identified single-use plastics from July 1, 2022 — items covered (exact list is UPSC-tested)
LiFE as the behavioural reinforcement framework for the SUP ban
Distinction: SUP ban is regulatory (Environment Protection Act, 1986); LiFE is voluntary
Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) under Plastic Waste Management Rules — link to LiFE goals

concepts.name: Energy Conservation and LiFE: LED and UJALA Connection
key_dimensions: UJALA scheme (Unnat Jyoti by Affordable LEDs for All) as a pre-existing LiFE-aligned initiative
Star labelling by Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) — consumer-facing energy conservation
LiFE's 'Save Energy' theme vs. Energy Conservation Act 2022 amendments — complementarity
UPSC trap: BEE is under Ministry of Power, not MoEFCC — institutional overlap

concepts.name: Water Conservation Under LiFE
key_dimensions: LiFE's 'Save Water' theme and its alignment with Jal Shakti Abhiyan and Catch the Rain campaign
Distinction: Jal Jeevan Mission focuses on supply; LiFE focuses on demand-side conservation
India's water stress indicators (per capita availability declining below 1700 m³ threshold)
Individual actions promoted: rainwater harvesting, greywater reuse, fixing leaks

concepts.name: Sustainable Food Systems and LiFE
key_dimensions: Promotion of millets (International Year of Millets 2023) as a LiFE-aligned sustainable food choice
Reducing food waste: India ranks among top food-wasting nations globally
Plant-based diets' lower carbon footprint — LiFE's implicit dietary nudge and its political sensitivity
Overlap with Zero Hunger (SDG-2) and Climate Action (SDG-13)

concepts.name: E-Waste Reduction Under LiFE
key_dimensions: India is the third-largest e-waste generator globally — scale of the problem
E-Waste Management Rules 2022: EPR framework for producers — regulatory vs. LiFE's voluntary approach
Individual actions: repair over replace, responsible disposal at authorised collection centres
UPSC trap: E-Waste rules are under MoEFCC via Environment Protection Act; LiFE is a mission — same ministry, different instruments

concepts.name: LiFE and Circular Economy Principles
key_dimensions: Circular economy: reduce, reuse, recycle — alignment with LiFE's consumption themes
India's draft National Resource Efficiency Policy and its relationship with LiFE
Contrast: linear economy model (take-make-dispose) vs. circular model advocated by LiFE
EU Circular Economy Action Plan comparison — India's voluntary approach vs. EU's regulatory approach

concepts.name: Behavioural Economics and Nudge Theory in LiFE
key_dimensions: LiFE explicitly uses nudge theory (Thaler & Sunstein) — making pro-environment choice the default/easy choice
Examples: defaulting to no plastic straw, opt-out linen change in hotels
Limitations of nudges: ineffective against structural poverty, availability gaps, and price barriers
Comparison with UK's Behavioural Insights Team ('Nudge Unit') — India's adaptation

concepts.name: LiFE and Climate Justice / Equity Concerns
key_dimensions: LiFE's target of 'mindful consumption' primarily relevant to middle/upper-income consumers — exclusion of the poor
India's Common But Differentiated Responsibilities (CBDR) stance: developed nations must lead consumption reduction
Risk of narrative inversion: poor nations blamed for consumption when historical emissions are from rich nations
LiFE as India's soft counter-argument to Western pressure on coal phase-down

concepts.name: LiFE in the Context of G20 and India's Climate Diplomacy
key_dimensions: India's G20 Presidency (Dec 2022–Nov 2023): LiFE as a signature deliverable
Voice of Global South Summit and LiFE as a developing-country-led climate narrative
Contrast with traditional climate diplomacy (finance, technology transfer) — LiFE adds a cultural/behavioural dimension
New Delhi Declaration's mention of LiFE — non-binding nature and diplomatic significance

concepts.name: Monitoring, Evaluation, and Metrics for LiFE
key_dimensions: Challenge: LiFE's outcomes (behaviour change) are difficult to quantify unlike NDC targets
Proposed indicators: number of pledges, reduction in per capita waste, energy saved per household
Absence of a statutory/legal framework for LiFE — purely mission/programme mode, not Act-backed
UPSC trap: LiFE has no dedicated legislation, unlike Environment Protection Act or Forest Conservation Act

concepts.name: Intersection of LiFE with National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC)
key_dimensions: NAPCC (2008): eight national missions — none explicitly on consumption behaviour
LiFE fills the 'demand-side' gap in NAPCC's supply-side focus (solar, energy efficiency, etc.)
Whether LiFE should be integrated as a ninth mission under NAPCC — a live policy debate
State Action Plans on Climate Change (SAPCCs) and potential integration of LiFE at state level
